A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same token-merging research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting and genomic-classification experiments, including MSE, accuracy, acceleration measurements, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports additional decoder-merging evaluations, Mamba and PatchTST experiments, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: V1 restricts transformer merging to encoders. V2 introduces decoder merging using adjacent-token merges with k=1 and final unmerging by cloning tokens. It also extends the existing single-sample dynamic procedure to batches by averaging threshold-derived merging counts across batch elements.

E1.justification: The five forecasting datasets and mouse genomic-classification task are retained. V2 adds controlled linear-trend and periodic-signal inputs for tracing merges in Chronos base (Appendix B.2, Figure 8), providing a limited expansion of test scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated local-pruning comparator against merging for Chronos small on ETTh1 (Appendix E.2, Figure 16); v1 discussed pruning without reporting this comparison. Existing unmerged-model, global-merging, and Gaussian-filter comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The main transformer evaluation changes from encoder-only to encoder-plus-decoder merging, with separate merging parameters and 185 inference-search trials instead of 180. V2 adds batch-size-10 dynamic evaluation, best-accuracy state-space configurations, and Mamba/PatchTST settings. Core data splits, forecasting horizons, and validation/test separation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds spectral-entropy/THD and token-representation analyses, cosine-versus-L1/L2 ablations, pruning comparisons, patch-tokenization tests, and tracing of merges on trend and periodic inputs. These substantially expand investigation of when and why merging works. The earlier smoothing, input-length, and positional-embedding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 2024, two timing warm-ups, two measurement runs per batch, and timing standard deviations generally below 2%. These disclosures move partly into Appendix C; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training uncertainty reporting appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises numerous results under the decoder-enabled procedure: for example, 10-layer Non-stationary Transformer acceleration on ETTm1 changes from 3.60× to 3.80× under changed merging conditions. Table 3 adds accuracy-oriented Hyena results (1.68×, 80.6%) and Mamba results, including 4.09× at 74.4% accuracy. PatchTST and diagnostic results are new; Chronos Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The local-similarity definition, complexity formula, and attention-only speed-up bound retain the same derivations (v1 Appendix A.1; v2 Appendix B.1). The added causality and Markov discussion supplies conceptual arguments, without new formal proofs or revised mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion add the claimed first causal merging scheme for transformer decoders and prediction of merging benefits from spectral properties without downstream evaluation. These substantially extend the contributions beyond v1's encoder-focused investigation. The headline Chronos acceleration claim is retained.

C2.justification: V2 extends the existing low-pass-filter hypothesis with interpretations involving spectral noise, learned token similarity, tokenization, and temporal inductive biases. Dynamic merging is recommended for small batches beyond v1's single-sample recommendation. The limitations remove the encoder restriction and also drop the acknowledgment of untested distribution-shift/adversarial robustness without adding such tests.

D1.justification: V2 specifies decoder insertion between self-attention and cross-attention, separate encoder/decoder merging parameters, and reuse of Hyena settings for Mamba. Resource estimates change from 80 to 100 A6000 hours for pretrained-model experiments and from 6 to 12 A100 hours for state-space experiments. Most existing training and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused comparisons with sparse attention, token skipping, and spectrum-preserving merging, citing Child, Raposo, and Tran respectively. It also distinguishes its decoder unmerging from Bolya and Hoffman. Most earlier related work survives in Appendix A; the Geisler graph reference and two Schwinn robustness references are removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract and contribution framing, reorganizes experiments into Results and Further investigations, and condenses the main related-work section while retaining an expanded appendix version. The appendices are reorganized into A–E, and the input-token redundancy discussion moves out of the main text.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Retained plots are resized, rearranged, and relabeled; the combined redundancy/dynamic figure is separated. Table 3 expands to two architectures and two objectives, alongside new diagnostic tables and figures.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses the explicit encoder-only restriction with a documented decoder procedure and empirical evaluation. New pruning, similarity, tokenization, and Mamba comparisons substantially strengthen support for applicability and design choices. These gains outweigh the qualifications: reliable spectral prediction remains supported only by associations across five existing datasets, and the removed robustness caveat remains unresolved.
